subject: Ornith variant intake: priority alignment, compatibility checks, and provisional version hold
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request to prioritize Ornith variant intake + provisional pin

Team —

Helios Labs just completed a model drop (internal name: Ornith) and product has a pilot that needs the "ornith-lite-v1" variant onboarded into staging next week. Before we proceed with full intake I want to align on two things:

1) Compatibility risk assessment — Laura / infra, can you run a quick parity test across tokenization/embedding drift and KV-cache behavior? Product is seeing ~4% answer divergence vs our baseline on a 50-sample eval set.

2) Provisional pin & routing policy — if the parity check fails in staging, I want to provisionally pin customer-facing routes to the current fallback model (meridian-3b) while we triage. That means we need a short temporary pin window (48–72 hrs) and a clear rollback/canary plan.

Ask: please confirm feasibility and provide ETA for the parity report (tokenizer parity + 100-request streaming pass) and whether you recommend a temporary pin. If we go ahead, we also need a minimal telemetry set to track quality regressions (top-5 intents, avg latency, token delta).

Attachments: ornith-intake-checklist.pdf — product-provided spec and sample prompts.

Thanks —
Vanessa
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request to prioritize Ornith variant intake + provisional pin

Vanessa —

Quick update from the runtime/interop side after a first pass on the intake checklist and the sample prompts:

- Tokenizer differences: Ornith uses an updated BPE merge table; we observed tokenization shifts that change prompt segmentation for ~18% of the sample prompts. This explains some of the answer divergence.
- Embedding drift: initial embeddings (CLS-like) show systematic drift on a subset of semantic categories. Need a 1000-sample embedding parity run to be confident.
- KV cache: runtime pathways are compatible but Ornith's attention cache layout introduces a different key ordering for multihead shapes; the runtime supports remapping but we need to validate correctness under our continuous-batching path.

I attached a short failure trace (sample-failure-trace.txt) and a zipped parity log with the initial 200-sample run. My recommendation:

- Run a full tokenizer parity + 1k embedding sample test (overnight)
- If drift > 2.5% on meaningful labels, recommend temporary pin while we (a) add tokenization normalization and (b) re-run quantization parity
- Canary plan: east region only, 1% traffic for 48 hours, automated rollback on intent-level regression > 3% or latency 2x baseline

ETA: I can get the full parity artifacts by EOD Wednesday (2026-08-12) if we prioritize infra runners.

Laura
Senior Build Engineer — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request to prioritize Ornith variant intake + provisional pin

On Tue, Aug 11, 2026 at 11:03 AM Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> Vanessa —
> 
> Quick update from the runtime/interop side after a first pass on the intake checklist and the sample prompts:
> 
> - Tokenizer differences: Ornith uses an updated BPE merge table; we observed tokenization shifts that change prompt segmentation for ~18% of the sample prompts. This explains some of the answer divergence.
> - Embedding drift: initial embeddings (CLS-like) show systematic drift on a subset of semantic categories. Need a 1000-sample embedding parity run to be confident.
> - KV cache: runtime pathways are compatible but Ornith's attention cache layout introduces a different key ordering for multihead shapes; the runtime supports remapping but we need to validate correctness under our continuous-batching path.

Agree with Laura. Additional notes from applied ML: quantization path (int8) appears to increase semantic drift for Ornith relative to float32 — hypothesis is that a slightly different layer ordering and fused ops cause small value shifts that compound after decoding. Steps I propose:

- Run float32 vs quantized parity on the same 1k samples (both embeddings and generation) — this will tell us whether we need a special quantization profile for Ornith.
- Enable KV-cache remap test harness under our heavy-batching simulation (we have a runner in infra labeled "batch-sim-03").
- If parity fails on either, implement a provisional hold: Pin production routes for the affected customer(s) to meridian-3b for up to 72 hours; use a canary in us-east with 1% traffic.

Requesting product confirmation: priority level (P0/P1) and permission to create the temporary pin. If P0, we will start parity runs tonight and aim for actionable artifacts within 24 hours.

—Priyom
Applied ML — Model Integration
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jennifer Hsu <jennifer.hsu@helios.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request to prioritize Ornith variant intake + provisional pin — approved provisional hold and action items

Thanks for the fast triage here. I'm authorizing the following today so we can keep Helios's pilot on schedule while limiting customer exposure:

1) Priority: P0 for parity and KV-cache validation — Priyom, please kick off the float32 vs quant run tonight and share artifacts to the INF-4821 ticket.
2) Provisional pin: approved for customer-facing routes tied to the Helios pilot. Pin window: up to 72 hours; we will auto-unpin after validation passes unless we extend by exception. Engineering, please implement a canary (us-east, 1% traffic) for 48 hours before expanding to broader staging.
3) Telemetry: minimal set is required before canary: top-5 intent accuracy, avg latency, token-count delta, error-rate by route. Laura, mark which logs we need to keep for 7 days.
4) Communication: Vanessa, please inform Helios of the temporary pin and the plan to run parity; cc'ing Jennifer so she has visibility. Do not promise a date beyond the 72-hr window.

I will loop in legal if licensing/terms come up; for now, proceed with the technical path. Priyom/Laura — update INF-4821 and drop the parity artifacts to the Drive link so CS and product can review.

Karthik
VP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: ornith-parity-logs.zip
